Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board (Board) on any matter listed on the
agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. If you wish to address the
Board, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Secretary. The Board will hear public comment
on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Board will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during
the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances
exist. The Board may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Board meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Board:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Board as a whole and not directed to individual Board members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services offered by this City,
please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire
to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a
disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Board regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted will also be made available
for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the Community Development Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular business
hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5744. You may also contact the City Clerk via

  JUNE 26, 2024

Chair Apodaca called the special meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers. Responding to roll call were Board Member Barragan, Board Member
Garcia, Vice Chair Lopez and Chair Apodaca. Board Member Navas was absent. Also
present were John P. Ramirez, Director of Community Development; Gabriela Garcia,
Senior Management Analyst; Dolores Bustamante, Senior Code Compliance Inspector;
and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

REORGANIZATION OF THE BOARD

By unanimous voice vote, Linda Lopez was appointed as Chair, and Rosa Barragan was
appointed as Vice-Chair of the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals
Board for the upcoming year.

MEETING MINUTES

The Board approved the minutes of the Special Property Maintenance and Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board Meeting of June 8, 2023.

REPORT OF DELINQUENT TRASH COLLECTION ACCOUNTS
Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Gabriela Garcia, Senior
Management Analyst, presented a report stating that the City of Norwalk provides
mandatory refuse service to protect the public health and welfare of its residents; that, as
such, Athens Services picks up trash weekly billing customers on a quarterly basis; that
payment for services is due within thirty (30) days from the billing date; that a late fee of
$25.00 is added if payment has not been made by the end of the service quarter; that the
hauler makes attempts during the year to collect on past-due accounts; that as authorized
in the Municipal Code, the hauler is allowed to seek payment through the tax rolls in July
of each year for the period of May 1st of the previous year through April 30th of the current
year; that in May of this year, 2,493 notices were prepared and mailed to all property
owners with a delinquent balance as of April 30, 2024; that the delinquent amounts totaled
$436,068; that since the notices went out, some delinquent accounts have been paid and
payments will continue to be received until July 31st; and that staff recommends that the
Board forward the delinquent properties to City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance
is paid by July 31st, 2024.

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Lopez closed the public
hearing.

year’s amount, and he asked what is the amount that is being recovered by the city, Ms.

EMERGENCY BOARD-UP COSTS
Report on the cost of emergency board-ups and the hearing of any objections of
property owners liable to be assessed for such abatement in accordance with the
provisions of Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.
Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.
Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Dolores Bustamante, Senior
Code Compliance Inspector, presented a report stating that this is the annual report on
the cost of emergency board-ups for the work performed for the fiscal year 2022-2023
and 2023-2024; that, as required, the property owners were provided with a notice and,
in addition, a “Declaration of Substandard” was filed with the Los Angeles County
Recorder’s Office; that two (2) properties received a notice; that the fiscal year delinquent
amount totaled $9,198.62 and $5,597.61, respectively; and that this evening they are
asking the Board to recommend City Council forward the amounts indicated for these
properties to be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll, unless the balances are paid
prior to August 1, 2024.
Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Lopez closed the public
hearing.
It was moved by Board Member Apodaca and seconded by Board Member Garcia to
direct staff to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that
the delinquent amount be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding
balance is paid prior to August 1, 2024.

SUBJECT: PUBLIC HEARING – REPORT OF DELINQUENT TRASH COLLECTION
  ACCOUNTS

Background:

City procedures state that any owner who has a delinquent account as of May 1, 2025 which
covers the period of May 1, 2024 to April 30, 2025 shall be sent, by mail, written notification that
the Appeals Board will review all such delinquent accounts during a public hearing. On May 1,
2025, Athens Services, the City’s solid waste hauler, mailed 2,122 notices that sought a
combined amount of $396,923. As of June 4, 2025, there are 907 accounts that have not settled
their account, with a combined balance of $231,694.90.

Daily payments and/or adjustments are being processed and will continue through July 31, 2025.
A City administrative fee of $25 will be added to each delinquent account not paid by July 31,
2025.

Fiscal Impact:

The City will be reimbursed $25 for each account on the final lien list for administrative
costs. The total amount will not be known until the final list is complete on July 31, 2025.

Citizens Advised:

Notices were mailed to all delinquent account holders by May 1, 2025 and posted at the City’s
three designated places and published in The Norwalk Patriot on May 30, 2025.

AUTHORITY

Section 15.32.150.E of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board to hold hearings related to work completed on private
properties to eliminate a hazard or to remove an unsafe condition or take any action that
would result in a cost assessment against the property.

Section 15.32.150.A of the NMC declares buildings public nuisances, if they are found
“structurally unsafe or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitute a fire
hazard, or are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use
constitute a hazard to safety or health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate
maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence, fire hazard, disaster damage, or abandonment,
as specified in this Code or in any other effective ordinance or statute.” Further such
buildings shall be abated by repair, rehabilitation, improvement, removal, or demolition,
in whole or part, in accordance with the procedures specified in the NMC.

Section 15.32.170 of the NMC authorizes the Building Official to serve as the record
owner and person having control of buildings that are deemed unsafe and pose a safety
hazard to the adjacent community and accords the Building Official authority to prevent
unauthorized persons from gaining access to such structures.

Section 15.32.170.12 of the NMC establishes emergency procedures for the Building
Official to remedy immediate hazards to unsafe buildings or structures by limiting access
to such buildings or structures by order of Sheriff, Public Safety Director, or the Chief of
the Fire Department after giving such notice to the record owner or person in charge or
both as circumstances permit or without any notice if immediate action is necessary.

BACKGROUND:

Staff takes emergency action to secure or otherwise abate the hazardous conditions to
protect the public whenever unsafe conditions are found to create a hazard to safety,
health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, fire hazard,
disaster damage, vandalism or abandonment.

When the City steps into secure properties and incurs a cost, the property owner on
record is sent an invoice for such work. Unpaid invoices are processed as a special
assessment to the property. Further, a “Declaration of Substandard” is filed with the Los
Angeles County Recorder’s Office as part of the nuisance abatement process to notify
interested parties of the pending cost associated with the abatement.

The purpose of the meeting tonight is to provide the opportunity for any interested party
to voice their concerns or objections to such assessments before the Board.

DISCUSSION:

Notice of the abatement expenses are sent as an invoice to the property owners of record.
Staff keeps an account of the abatement expenses and maintains the list of unpaid
invoices as an itemized written report to the Property Maintenance and Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board for confirmation (Attachment No. 1). Property owners liable
to assessment may bring objections of such assessments before the Board.

The Board shall hear all objections or protests of property owners liable to be assessed
for the delinquent fees and may make revisions to the report and recommendations to the
City Council with regard to disposition of the delinquent fees.

Upon the recommendation of the Board and confirmation by the City Council, the cost of
abatement will constitute a lien on the property and may be paid to the Director of Finance
prior to August 1, 2025. The unpaid liens will be delivered to the County Auditor to be
collected at the time and in the manner of other taxes on the property.

Attachment No. 1 details the properties that were invoiced for emergency board-up
performed pursuant to Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code for which
